problem: Existing VLN and ObjectNav methods need step-by-step instructions or fixed object categories. They cannot parse high-level intent (e.g. 'I want coffee') or localize open-vocabulary objects under spatial constraints in large real indoor scenes.
motivation: Real human requests are abstract and involve spatial relations ('fruit on the left of the tea room'). Closing this gap requires both commonsense reasoning about where a target object lies and fine-grained spatial-aware pointing. General VLMs get near-zero success on this task.
key_idea: A hierarchical global-to-local framework: a Reasoning-VLM (GPT-4o) picks the target object and room from an annotated top-down 3D map, and a Pointing-VLM (NaviAfford, trained on 1.0M spatial-affordance samples) explores waypoints and localizes the exact object.
insight: Both stages matter. Removing map or room-level annotation drops avg SR from 68.0% to 36-40%, so semantic annotations are what let the Reasoning-VLM place objects in rooms. Swapping NaviAfford for general VLMs (GPT-4o 32.0%, Qwen2.5-VL-72B 16.0%) or RoboPoint (57.5%) shows that affordance-specific pointing training is what converts reasoning into navigation success.
method: Task and 3D scene construction: LiDAR mobile-device RGB scans are reconstructed into a point cloud and mesh, then converted to a top-down map; success means within 1 m of the target with line of sight.

Global policy (Reasoning-VLM): GPT-4o gets the instruction plus a room/region-annotated top-down view (MapNav-style annotation) with a structured prompt. It infers the target object O* and the most likely region R*, then a random waypoint is sampled in R*.

NaviAfford (Pointing-VLM): Qwen2.5-VL-7B fully fine-tuned with SFT to output point coordinates, on ~50K images and 1.0M QA pairs built from LVIS and Where2Place. Data includes object affordance (directional relations) and spatial affordance (free space).

Local navigation: at each waypoint the agent captures panoramic RGB by rotating, and NaviAfford points at the target. The mean of the predicted points is back-projected with depth and camera intrinsics into robot/world coordinates for navigation.

Exploration fallback: if the target is not found, Reasoning-VLM reads the local map and history to decide whether to keep exploring the area or switch rooms. NaviAfford proposes the next exploration point when the agent stays.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, Reasoning-VLM) + NaviAfford (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, fully fine-tuned, Pointing-VLM)
setting.training_data: 1.0M QA pairs on ~50K images from LVIS and Where2Place (object and spatial affordance pointing); GPT-4o zero-shot
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with panoramic rotational scans, plus a global annotated top-down 3D scene map and a local top-down map
setting.action_space: waypoints on a top-down map, with pixel-to-robot coordinate conversion for navigation to the target
setting.privileged: pre-built annotated global 3D scene map (pre-scanned with LiDAR, with room-level annotations)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 real scenes (Meeting Room A/B, Tea Room, Workstation, Balcony), 10 tasks each, 50 tasks total; 5 trials per task per the metrics section
numbers.extra: pre-built annotated 3D scene map; success radius 1 m; baselines given the top-down map
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Avg. SR 66.4%; per-scene SR 72.0/64.0/60.0/76.0/60.0; Meeting Room A NE 1.23 (Meeting Room B 1.45, Tea Room 1.89, Workstation 1.56, Balcony 1.34)

numbers_note: Custom real-world benchmark only, no standard benchmarks. The ablation tables report an avg SR of 68.0% for the same full system on Tea Room and Workstation only, which differs from the 66.4% five-scene average in Table 1. Table 1 NE is reported per scene, with no overall average.
results: NavA3 reaches an average SR of 66.4% across 5 real scenes with NE of 1.23-1.89 m. The strongest baseline, MapNav*, gets 25.2%, and general VLMs (GPT-4o etc.) get 0-2.8%. NaviAfford reaches 63.2% average pointing accuracy vs RoboPoint's 50.2%, and the system deploys on RealMan wheeled and Unitree Go2 quadruped robots.
limitations: Evaluation is only on a self-built, small real-world benchmark (5 scenes, 50 tasks) with no standard public benchmarks. Baselines are adapted or modified, so comparisons may not be fully fair.
Requires a pre-scanned, room-annotated 3D map of the environment and a GPT-4o API for reasoning, which limits generalization to unseen or dynamic environments.
Main-text numbers are inconsistent across tables (66.4% vs 68.0% for the same system). The dataset and code are only promised.
